title: Russia Launches 200+ Drones Across 14 Regions — 5 Killed Including 3 in Rivne, 2 in Kryvyi Rih
detail: Russia launched one of the largest drone campaigns of the post-ceasefire period on May 13, 2026, sending over 200 Shahed-type drones at Ukraine in multiple waves targeting 14 regions simultaneously. The overnight wave alone included 139 drones, of which Ukraine's air defenses neutralized 111 via interception and electronic jamming. In Rivne Oblast, a drone struck a residential building — killing 3 people and injuring 4 others. In Kryvyi Rih, 2 people were killed and 4 wounded in a direct drone strike. In Odesa, drone debris fell near a 9-story residential building, igniting a fire that burned several parked cars. Power was cut to six regions near the front lines. Ukrainian military intelligence warned of a possible follow-up wave of cruise and ballistic missiles. A second daytime wave of 168 Shahed drones was tracked by Ukraine's 'Monitor' service starting at 11:27 local time, with additional waves following throughout the afternoon. The scale of the attack came just 30+ hours after Russia's similar 216-drone campaign on May 12, confirming Moscow's intent to sustain maximum aerial pressure after the collapsed Trump-brokered ceasefire.

media.caption: Russia launches 200+ Shahed drones across 14 Ukrainian regions on May 13, 2026 — Rivne residential building hit, 3 killed

title: Trump Says Ukraine Peace Deal 'Getting Very Close' — Kremlin Contradicts, Russia Resumes Mass Strikes
detail: As Trump departed the White House for a summit in Beijing on May 13, 2026, he told reporters that a Ukraine-Russia peace settlement was 'getting very close,' stating: 'The end of the war in Ukraine, I really think, is getting very close... Believe it or not, it's getting closer, and we think we're going to end up getting a settlement between Russia and Ukraine.' The statement came as Russia simultaneously launched 200+ drones across Ukraine. The Kremlin explicitly contradicted Trump's timeline, calling a peace deal 'a very long road, full of complex details.' Zelensky's camp said the two sides were '90% agreed' on a 20-point peace framework but that territorial issues — Russia's demand for the remainder of Donetsk Oblast — remained the core impasse. Ukraine's foreign minister reiterated that no territorial concessions would be accepted without binding security guarantees from NATO or equivalent powers. Discussions were reported about a potential Putin-Zelensky meeting in a neutral third country, but the Kremlin insisted this could only occur after a full peace treaty was finalized — a condition Ukraine said was circular.

media.caption: Trump says Ukraine peace deal 'getting very close' as Russia resumes mass drone attacks — May 13, 2026

title: Ukraine Strikes Russian Gas Facilities in Orenburg (~1,500 km Deep) — Russia Claims 286 Ukrainian Drones Shot Down
detail: Ukraine struck gas infrastructure facilities in Russia's Orenburg region on May 13, 2026 — approximately 1,500 kilometers from Ukrainian territory, one of the deepest long-range drone strikes of the war. Russia's defense ministry reported shooting down 286 Ukrainian drones over Russian territory overnight, suggesting a large-scale coordinated Ukrainian drone campaign targeting multiple Russian regions simultaneously. The Orenburg strike targeted key natural gas processing facilities connected to Russia's export pipeline network. The depth of the strike demonstrated the ongoing expansion of Ukraine's drone range and its strategic doctrine of disrupting Russian energy export revenues and domestic fuel supply chains. Russia simultaneously claimed its own air defenses intercepted Ukrainian drones across multiple oblasts.

media.caption: Ukraine strikes Russian gas facilities in Orenburg — one of Ukraine's deepest long-range drone strikes (~1,500 km), May 13, 2026

title: 170+ Combat Engagements Across Frontline — Kharkiv and Pokrovsk Directions Most Active
detail: Ukraine's General Staff reported 170 combat engagements since the start of May 13, 2026 — one of the highest daily counts since the ceasefire collapsed. The fighting was concentrated in two main operational directions: In the South Slobozhansky/Kharkiv direction, clashes were reported near Vovchansk, Starytsya, Krasne Pershe, Zelene, Ternova, Petro-Ivanivka, Myrove, Symynivka, Prylipka, and Lyman. In the Pokrovsk direction, combat was ongoing near Toretske, Bilytske, Pokrovsk, Rodynske, Hryshyne, Kotlyne, Udachne, Molodetske, Muravka, and Novopidhorodnie. Geolocated footage confirmed Russian advances in the Sotnytskyi Kozachok area northwest of Kharkiv and northeast of Orikhovo-Vasylivka near the E40 highway. The Kerch Bridge (Crimea Bridge) was also closed to traffic after explosions and drone activity were reported in occupied Crimea overnight. Aurora 26, a NATO exercise involving 18,000 troops from 11 allies and Ukraine, concluded on May 13 — focusing on FPV drones, reconnaissance UAVs, and drone interception at Swedish training grounds and Gotland island.

media.caption: 170+ combat engagements across Ukraine frontline — Kharkiv and Pokrovsk directions, May 13, 2026
